what_its_for: Vismodegib is a cancer medicine used to treat adults with a type of skin cancer called basal cell carcinoma. It is used when the cancer has spread to other parts of the body, or when it cannot be treated with surgery or radiation. It works by blocking a signal in the body (called the Hedgehog pathway) that helps cancer cells grow.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsule whole with or without food. Do not open, crush, or chew the capsule. Try to take it at the same time each day. Wash your hands after handling the capsule.
dosing: The usual dose is one 150 mg capsule taken by mouth once every day. Always follow your doctor's instructions and do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip the missed dose and just take your next dose at your regular time the following day. Do not take two doses in one day to make up for the one you missed.
storage: Store vismodegib capsules at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep the capsules in the original bottle with the lid tightly closed. Keep this medicine away from heat, moisture, and light. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicines down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about safe disposal.
what_to_avoid: Do not donate blood or blood products while taking this medicine and for at least 24 months after your last dose. Do not donate sperm while taking this medicine and for 3 months after your last dose. Women must not become pregnant — use two effective forms of birth control during treatment and for 24 months after the last dose, as this drug can cause serious birth defects or loss of the baby. Men must use condoms during treatment and for 3 months after the last dose, even if they have had a vasectomy. Avoid breastfeeding during treatment and for 24 months after the last dose. Talk to your doctor before taking any new medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as some can affect how vismodegib works.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience any of the following: severe muscle spasms or cramps, unusual or severe muscle pain, weakness, nausea or vomiting that is severe or does not go away, significant weight loss or loss of appetite, hair loss that is bothersome, changes in your sense of taste or loss of taste, tiredness that is extreme or gets worse, signs of pregnancy (missed period, unusual breast tenderness), or any new or worsening symptoms. Call your doctor if you have trouble swallowing the capsule or have any concerns about side effects.
when_it_works: You may not feel any different right away. Cancer medicines like vismodegib work over time, and your doctor will check your progress with regular appointments and tests. Do not stop taking the medicine without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel well.
special_populations: Pregnancy: This drug is NEVER safe to use during pregnancy. It can cause death of the unborn baby or serious birth defects. Women who could become pregnant must use two reliable forms of birth control. Men: Use condoms during treatment and for 3 months after stopping. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in children or teenagers under 18. Older adults: No specific dose changes are needed for older adults, but talk to your doctor about any other health conditions you have.
